body:
Agreed, we should avoid setting `reportItem["isRange"]` to true if either of `usageMinimum` or `usageMaximum` is missing. The purpose of `isRange` is to indicate whether to use `usageMinimum`/`usageMaximum` or the `usages` array for this item. It's possible that a malformed descriptor might only have `usageMinimum` or `usageMaximum`, in this case we should not use a default value of 0 and should set `isRange` to false, even if `usages` is empty.

A malformed descriptor could have both usage min/max and non-empty `usages`, in this case I think we should prefer to set `isRange` to true and leave `usages` undefined. It's not clear to me if it's better to keep the min/max or `usages` in this case but since the device descriptor is malformed I think it doesn't matter. 

A valid descriptor could have usage min == usage max, in this case we should set `isRange` to true.

I think your proposed steps satisfy all of these.
